guide.summary: The app can use a public OAuth integration where each customer authorizes its own Notion user and selects pages to share. The read-only boundary comes from the Read content capability, which covers page and block reads but not page creation or modification.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of Notion pages that customers explicitly share with the app. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Public OAuth 2.0 authorization for customer-selected pages
findings.detail: Notion documents OAuth 2.0 for public integrations: the user is sent to the authorization URL, selects pages, returns with a code, and the app exchanges it at the token endpoint. Authorization can start once client credentials and the redirect URI are configured; Marketplace submission or review is not required.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own Notion account and shares pages with the app.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading page titles and content
findings.detail: The Read content capability lets a connection read existing content, including page retrieval and markdown content retrieval. Missing capability returns 403. This capability does not allow page creation or updates.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads page titles or page content through the Notion API.

findings.title: Customer must share pages during the authorization flow
findings.detail: Only pages the customer selects in the page picker are granted, and the user needs full access to share them. Pages not shared return 404 or are unavailable; a child page is accessible when its parent is shared. Only the authorizing user can share with the app.
findings.appliesWhen: A customer expects the app to read specific pages.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration with read-only capability and redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Notion Developer portal, create an OAuth integration with installation scope set to Any workspace, configure the redirect URI, and set capabilities to Read content only. Store the client ID and secret from the Configuration tab in environment variables.
steps.doneWhen: The integration has a client ID, client secret, authorization URL, a configured redirect URI, and only the Read content capability enabled.

steps.title: Read a shared test page's properties to obtain its title
steps.detail: Call Retrieve a page with the shared test page ID. The page title is found in the title-type property whose key is commonly Name or title; read the title array's plain_text.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns the test page object and its title plain_text matches the expected title. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.doneWhen: Every returned unknown block ID has been fetched or reported as inaccessible, and no further truncation remains.
